correctness.rationale: The action is free by row uniqueness. Orbit cells and their attaching words are derived directly; \(3n-6\) homotopy-preserving generator/two-cell eliminations leave one generator and (n-2)(n-4) relators of degree zero or minus n, with at least one nonzero. Nielsen transformations of the wedge-of-circles attaching map give exactly M(Z/n,1) wedge (\(n^2-6n+7\)) two-spheres. The proof establishes this for all n>=5 without finite extrapolation; a standalone script corroborates quotient boundaries, modular ranks, and substitution indices.

evidence: Shareshian–Wachs 2004 Theorem 1.1 gives connectivity of the original complex. Friedman–Hanlon 1997 Theorem 1.2 gives its Betti numbers. Full RESULTS of the three-by-four column-subgroup surface classification and three-row capacity-two cyclic quotient were inspected.
broader_coverage.reasoning: No inspected theorem asserts the full two-dimensional cyclic-column quotient splitting for all ordinary three-by-n complexes, n>=5. The three-by-four study ends at n=4; the capacity-two study has a different face condition and dimension. Generic finite-cover reasoning gives less than this homotopy equivalence.

evidence: Existing n=4 C4 quotient is the Klein bottle. At n>=5 the original chessboard complex is 1-connected and 2-dimensional, and a cyclic column shift acts freely; these imply pi_1=C_n and permit Euler characteristic computation. The degree-n plus null-attaching-cell cofiber decomposition requires an additional explicit two-dimensional homotopy argument.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Older connectivity and character formulas imply only coarse invariants of Y_n, not a homotopy equivalence of CW complexes. The new proof explicitly cancels 3n-6 cell pairs and reduces every remaining two-cell attaching map to degree zero or n. Thus the complete homotopy splitting is not a corollary of the inspected results.

value.rationale: The natural full cyclic-column quotient family has an explicit complete two-dimensional homotopy classification for every n>=5. The Moore factor produces first homology of arbitrary cyclic order while the other \(n^2-6n+7\) independent two-dimensional classes split off as spheres; this is a structural homotopy result rather than the already accessible Euler/homology computation. It covers both prime and composite widths and identifies the post-torus transition.
